title: Disclosure of a consequential medical error
short_description: A hospitalized patient received an excessive medication dose because of a known infusion-pump programming error and developed severe hypotension before the error was recognized and corrected.
decision_question: After a known preventable medication error with uncertain downstream harm, what must the hospital disclose now and what information may wait for the investigation?
position_families: Disclose the known error promptly, explain known and possible consequences, apologize, identify uncertainty and schedule updates
Provide an immediate adverse-event disclosure of established facts while reserving statements about preventability, causal attribution and corrective responsibility until investigation supports them
Pair disclosure with an institutional response-and-resolution process including mitigation and later corrective-action reporting

scenario: A hospitalized patient received an excessive medication dose because of a known infusion-pump programming error and developed severe hypotension before the error was recognized and corrected. The patient is now stable, but clinicians do not yet know whether a new kidney abnormality will resolve or whether the error will have lasting effects. The programming error itself is established; the event investigation has not yet determined all contributing causes or preventability at the system level. The hospital must decide what to disclose immediately, including responsibility and apology, and what should be identified as uncertain and updated after investigation.
